reasons.text: Electricity bought is only 0.37x the minimum needed for the tonnes claimed (110 kWh/t against at least 300)
42% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
Category III share of certificates is 57%, +55% versus what its process route can produce
Sold products equal only 6% of the output expected from the tonnes claimed
100% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.32x the cost floor)
84% of high-value consignments have no e-way bill

inspection_checklist: Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
Cross-check the certificate generation dates and category mix against the plant's process route and stock registers.
Reconcile product sales with processed tonnes; contact the product buyers listed and verify that they received the material.
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
